title: Messaging
description: Can publish and consume so acks, retries and ordering are measured — and can state the actual delivery guarantee instead of claiming exactly-once.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can publish a message to a queue, consume it in a separate process, and point at ack versus nack — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can publish a domain event from an API, show the HTTP response returning before the consumer finishes, recover an unacked message after a crash, and route a poison message to an inspectable dead-letter path with a bounded retry.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently make duplicate delivery safe for domain state, write down the idempotency key, and compare RabbitMQ to Kafka on a named scenario — scoping ordering to a partition, not a brand.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a dual-write, ack-window or unclean-leader failure where 'at-least-once' alone would mislead, cite the lost or duplicated effect, and produce a results table another on-call can use without opening application source.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's topology, name a casual exactly-once claim or an unbounded retry, and teach when to trust a Kafka offset over a RabbitMQ ack (or the reverse) on an unfamiliar pipeline.
